Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old female with a multi-day, progressively worsening headache likely consistent with a migraine-like presentation; management discussed includes stronger analgesia and follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache started ~3 days ago, constant but with fluctuations; predominantly around the right eye; described as dull with intermittent sharpness; pain rated ~8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Light sensitivity (photophobia) with eye discomfort on brightness; nausea without vomiting; neck stiffness; difficulty focusing; no visual loss or weakness reported.
- Course: Headache worsened from day 1 to day 3 despite initial ibuprofen use; ibuprofen taken for 2 days, approx 3 tablets/day, with little relief.
- Past medical history: Not documented besides headaches; mother and sister have migraines; no prior personal migraine history reported.
- Medications: No regular medications. Acute ibuprofen use described (3 tablets/day for 2 days); eye glasses worn; no known drug allergies.
- Social history: Socially smokes and drinks; works in IT; increased work-related stress mentioned; lives with three housemates.
- Allergies: None known.

Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.

Impression:
- Probable migraine-type headache; family history of migraines supports this assessment; not yet definitively diagnosed.

Plan:
- Pain management: Discussed using a stronger analgesic regimen today. Options mentioned include Naproxen, Paracetamol, and Codeine; ibuprofen dosing could be optimized (up to two tablets, three times daily) with dose/route/frequency not documented in this visit.
- Medication plan: Prescribe stronger analgesia today (Naproxen or alternatives); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Adjunctive strategies: Consider keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.
- Follow-up: Schedule follow-up in about 1–2 weeks; return sooner if headaches worsen or new neurological symptoms develop (vision changes, weakness, etc.).
- Prophylaxis: If headaches become more frequent, discuss preventive therapy at the next visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Allergies; full medication reconciliation; vitals; neurologic/fundoscopic exam; pregnancy status (if relevant); imaging results if considered.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Some informal, repetitive speech; overall content sufficient to generate plan, though several details (dosage specifics for proposed meds) are not documented in the transcript.
